notes: Europe PMC preprint search for 'sequencing by expansion' returned only two SBX-relevant preprints. One is the Feb 2025 Roche technology paper (Kokoris et al., doi 10.1101/2025.02.19.639056). The other is the Broad single-cell isoform preprint (Georgescu et al., Jul 2026, doi 10.64898/2026.07.15.738809). The API record for the Broad preprint has no cost tables, no reads-per-cell figure, no Illumina comparison and no UMI/barcode accuracy figure. I did not read either full text: bioRxiv returned HTTP 429, and the Europe PMC query with AXELIOS and SBX returned 503, so only the narrower query ran. A later pass might still find cost data in the full-text methods. Nothing here is a third-party cost-per-sample table, and no independent Sanger, CNAG or Hartwig preprint turned up. The Broad authors include Roche staff (Kokoris, AlKhafaji, possibly others), so this is a vendor-collaboration paper, not an independent benchmark.
how_to_mine: Fetch the full text of 10.64898/2026.07.15.738809 (v2) from biorxiv.org and its supplementary tables. Retry after a delay to avoid the 429, or use the Europe PMC full-text endpoint /PPR/<id>/fullTextXML. Look for reads per cell, cells per run, the multiplexing level (which implies $/cell) and any Illumina short-read comparison. Re-run Europe PMC with 'AXELIOS' and 'SBX-S' separately, restricted to 2026 dates, to find Sanger, CNAG and Hartwig preprints. Low expected payoff.
new_candidates: Full text of Georgescu et al. (Broad/Roche), bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.15.738809: check cost-per-cell, reads per cell and the Illumina short-read comparison. 9.5B reads in a 2-hour run is the only scale data point.
Europe PMC search for 'AXELIOS' alone, and for 'SBX-S', limited to 2026 preprints, to find Sanger and CNAG evaluations.
